sections.sectionText: Topic: Documentary Documentary filmmakers and photographers are increasingly playing with the limits of fact and fiction. What is real? What is artificial? What is authentic and true? As boundaries blur and genres melt, the very definition of a 'documentary film' is coming into question. Our study will include discussion, viewing a lot of work, a few readings, and making short video documentaries.

sections.sectionText: Critical Media Practices: Art, Poetics, and Social Change. This course is based on the idea that art, while not directly changing the world, fosters critical reflection on its challenges. Students will explore how creative practice can act as a catalyst for transformation, engaging with films, readings, podcasts, site visits, and exercises across contemporary art, performance, poetry, and the humanities. This course is intended for students in the School of Art+Design. Any available seats left on December 1 will be made available to all Majors.

sections.sectionText: Seminar: Methods Criticism, or “Practical Theory” is a graduate seminar that provides a selection of critical texts for engaging the ideas, contexts, and practices of contemporary art, with a significant part of the course content oriented toward the research interests of the participants. This course will emphasize strategies for addressing critical theory from a practical perspective: theory as a useful tool for understanding and articulating one’s creative research and practice.
